digest.component_or_area: MCP HTTP server deployment on AWS infrastructure
propositions: A self-contained HTTP server for rebar MCP must be deployed on the AWS box (Gerrit + review-bot + opcert) to enable copilot, codex, and claude clients to drive all rebar operations through a standard interface.
The MCP server must be exposed through nginx /mcp/ TLS edge routing to loopback-bound rebar-mcp HTTP using static bearer token authentication with per-client PATs materialized from SSM.

Autodeploy must use blue-green immutable-release (build new image → start new container → health-check → atomic nginx upstream flip → retire old) instead of stop-and-drain to safely redeploy MCP without killing in-flight certified operations.

The MCP server must sign op-certs (plan-review and completion-verifier) under the existing opcert environment (env_id 9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65) already pinned in .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml, with completion-verifier enforcement proved by fixture tests but deferred for live configuration.
Per-client bearer PATs must be SSM-provisioned as code in ssm.tf, gitignored in client-config templates, and guarded by committed-secret tests to prevent accidental secret commits.

Copilot, codex, and claude must each be configured with static-bearer MCP credentials matching their current official documentation, and verified to execute basic rebar commands against the live endpoint.
